summary.headline: S.P. Apparels Q1 FY27 consolidated EBITDA rose 15.9% to INR 61.4 crore on revenue flat at INR 401 crore; FY27 guidance of INR 2,000 crore reiterated.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was broadly flat year-on-year at INR 401 crore (vs INR 403 crore), while EBITDA rose 15.9% to INR 61.4 crore and margin expanded to 15.3% from 13.1%. PAT grew 20.4% to INR 24.9 crore. Management attributed the soft top line to U.S. tariff-related order holding in March-May and customer-requested shipment deferrals, and said growth will be back-end weighted into H2 FY27. The company reiterated its INR 2,000 crore FY27 revenue guidance, and announced a INR 3 per share dividend and a proposed stock split from INR 10 to INR 2 face value.

guidance_outlook: FY27 consolidated revenue guidance of INR 2,000 crore reiterated; management expects H2 to be stronger and to recover the Q1 shortfall, though Q1 delivered only INR 400 crore.
Q2 FY27 revenue expected to be better than Q1 on the top line.
Garment division (incl. YBA and Sri Lanka) EBITDA margin guided above 15% for the full year.
Young Brand revenue guided to INR 340-350 crore for FY27 (FY26: about INR 300 crore).
Infant export value guided to INR 1,300-1,400 crore for FY27 (FY26: about INR 1,100 crore; call also cited INR 955 crore for the prior year).
Consolidated interest cost guided to INR 30-35 crore for the full year, excluding exchange loss; Q1 interest of about INR 15 crore included a INR 1.75 crore forex hit.
SPUK guidance of GBP 13 million+ in about 3 years and GBP 50 million in about 5 years; a later answer cited GBP 50-60 million in 3-5 years.
Sri Lanka revenue expected at INR 150-200 crore by end of March 2027, per CFO.
Sri Lanka stabilisation expected by about March 2027; job-work route could add 500-600 machines within a year.
capex_capacity: About 750 machines added in India in FY27 so far; utilisation fell YoY because of order slowness from U.S. tariff uncertainty in March-May.
Sri Lanka has about 1,650 machines (about 1,300 used for exports); management says it can go up to 2,000. Factories are fully running except one at 85-90%.
Salem facility started trial production last month; full Phase 1 capacity expected about three months after Diwali.
Sivakasi factory started; plan to add about 400 machines over two years.

Young Brand: Palladum facility in production; all planned units in commercial production by October; new bra line with about INR 10 crore investment, investment from September-October, full revenue next fiscal, orders for about 200 machines.
Total sewing capacity cited at about 10,000 machines (about 6,000 India, 2,000 Sri Lanka, 1,750 YBA).

SPAL booked until October and open for November onwards; YBA orders booked until January per management.
SPUK added three UK customers (two UK, one EU) and is adding three more; Marks & Spencer named as one of them.
UK-India FTA recently effective; UK customer engagement improving. The EU-India FTA is expected to be signed by end of FY27.
Management says customers are cautious about possible new U.S. legislation but are not currently expecting a negative impact.
Realisation per piece is product-mix driven, so no single average (INR 150/piece query) was accepted by management.

qa_highlights.question: Why was capacity utilisation lower (about 14% drop YoY), what was the air freight cost, and will shipment delays continue into Q2?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said about 750 machines were added in India this year, and utilisation fell because of order slowness linked to U.S. tariff uncertainty in March-May. Air freight in SPUK was about GBP 50,000. Management said there is no shipment spillover expected, and the delays were due to customer requests, not containers.

qa_highlights.question: Can the three new customers be named, and how large can SPUK become?
qa_highlights.answer: Names were withheld until first shipment; two new customers are UK and one EU. SPUK is adding three more large customers, with Marks & Spencer named as one. Guidance is GBP 13 million-plus in about 3 years and GBP 50 million in about 5 years. A later answer cited GBP 50-60 million in 3-5 years.

qa_highlights.question: Sri Lanka utilisation, revenue and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Factories are fully running except one at 85-90%, with pre-operative losses expected to clear by end-March 2027. One country manager and one CFO run the operations, with payments controlled from India. Sri Lanka revenue was INR 25 crore in Q1, and management expects INR 150-200 crore by end-March 2027.

qa_highlights.question: What is the new bra product line in Young Brand, and what investment is needed?
qa_highlights.answer: Molded value-added bras, with orders that can fill about 200 machines. Investment starts September-October, with an estimated maximum of INR 10 crore for machinery and team acquisition in an existing building. Full revenue is expected next fiscal year.

qa_highlights.question: Does the Q2-onward margin improve given tariff rollback? Is capex back on track for Salem and India?
qa_highlights.answer: Garment division EBITDA margin is guided above 15% for the full year, including Sri Lanka, and Q2 revenue is expected to be better than Q1. Management said Salem began trial production last month, with full Phase 1 capacity about three months after Diwali. Sivakasi has started, with about 400 more machines planned over two years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR 2,000 crore guidance achievable after Q1 revenue of about INR 400 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated the INR 2,000 crore target by end-March 2027, saying H2 will recover the Q1 shortfall. It did not give quarterly phasing. Yarn division EBITDA was about INR 7.5 crore in Q1.

qa_highlights.question: Order book, and why did YBA volume fall sequentially?
qa_highlights.answer: Order book is about INR 430 crore for SPAL, about INR 72-100 crore for YBA, and about INR 60-70 crore for SPUK, totalling about INR 570-600 crore. The figures were inconsistent across answers. YBA volume was 5 million pieces versus 5.2 million in the prior quarter, with customers holding orders for about 1-2 months awaiting tariff reversal.

qa_highlights.question: Is the 17.6% garment margin one-off, and what is realisation per piece?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no one-offs; the margin came from efficiency and product mix. Realisation per piece depends on product mix, so management did not accept a single average such as INR 150 per piece.

qa_highlights.question: Infant export and YBA FY27 volume guidance, and interest cost?
qa_highlights.answer: YBA revenue is guided to INR 340-350 crore (FY26: about INR 300 crore). Infant export value is guided to INR 1,300-1,400 crore (FY26: about INR 1,100 crore). Consolidated interest is guided to INR 30-35 crore for the full year, excluding forex; Q1 included a INR 1.75 crore forex hit.

qa_highlights.question: Are H2 growth and orders backed by bookings, and what is the U.S. outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: SPAL is booked until October and open from November, and YBA orders are booked until January. Customers are not currently expecting a negative impact from possible new U.S. legislation, but they are cautious about the outlook beyond three to four months.

risks_watch: Recovery of INR 2,000 crore FY27 revenue guidance: Q1 delivered about INR 400 crore, so H2 needs an average of roughly INR 530-550 crore per quarter.
U.S. tariff and possible new U.S. legislation: YBA is 100% U.S.-market, and customers have held back orders during tariff uncertainty.
SPUK profitability: EBITDA was negative INR 1.0 crore in Q1 on small air shipments and deferred shipments; the GBP 13 million and GBP 50 million targets depend on new customers converting.
Sri Lanka ramp-up: the company expects stabilisation by about March 2027, with revenue of INR 150-200 crore targeted by then.
Standalone revenue declined to INR 265.9 crore from INR 287.7 crore, while margin rose; the margin's sustainability depends on mix and utilisation recovery.
Order-book figures were inconsistent across the call (YBA INR 72 crore vs INR 100 crore; total INR 570-600 crore), so the disclosed backlog needs verification.
key_quotes: The first half is expected to remain moderate, but we expect a stronger revenue trajectory in the second half, supported by improved customer order inflows, U.K. FTA -related traction, normalization of shipment schedules and better operating intensity across our key business verticals.
What we lost in first quarter, we will be able to achieve in the second half.
And their shipment performance is perfect on time, everything.
No. There's nothing to do with one -off things, but the margins is purely with respect to the improved efficiency because there is a change in the product mix.
summary.management_tone: Confident on margins, guidance and the medium-term SPUK and Sri Lanka story, but cautious on near-term top line and U.S. tariff exposure. Management was vague on the quarterly phasing of the INR 2,000 crore target and gave inconsistent order-book numbers.
